title: Un favor
desc: Asking for something and owing something

sn.s: Necesito ayuda para mover un mueble.
sn.e: I need help moving a piece of furniture.

sn.s: Le pido el favor a don Beto.
sn.e: I ask don Beto the favour.

sn.s: "Don Beto, ¿me hace un favor?"
sn.e: "Don Beto, would you do me a favour?"

sn.s: "Diga", dice él.
sn.e: "Go on," he says.

sn.s: Le explico lo del mueble.
sn.e: I explain about the furniture.

sn.s: Don Beto deja lo que está haciendo.
sn.e: Don Beto leaves what he is doing.

sn.s: Viene conmigo sin pensarlo.
sn.e: He comes with me without thinking about it.

sn.s: Movemos el mueble en diez minutos.
sn.e: We move the furniture in ten minutes.

sn.s: "Muchas gracias, don Beto", digo yo.
sn.e: "Thank you very much, don Beto," I say.

sn.s: "No es nada", dice él.
sn.e: "It's nothing," he says.

sn.s: Y se va a seguir con lo suyo.
sn.e: And he goes back to what he was doing.

sn.s: Yo pienso que ahí terminó todo.
sn.e: I think that is the end of it.

sn.s: No terminó nada.
sn.e: It is not the end of anything.

sn.s: Dos semanas después don Beto me pide algo.
sn.e: Two weeks later don Beto asks me for something.

sn.s: Me pide que le cuide la casa una tarde.
sn.e: He asks me to watch his house one afternoon.

sn.s: Yo digo que sí, claro.
sn.e: I say yes, of course.

sn.s: Y ahí entiendo cómo funciona.
sn.e: And that is when I understand how it works.

sn.s: Aquí un favor no se paga con gracias.
sn.e: Here a favour is not paid for with thanks.

sn.s: Un favor se paga con otro favor.
sn.e: A favour is paid for with another favour.

sn.s: Pero no enseguida.
sn.e: But not immediately.

sn.s: Devolver el favor enseguida sería feo.
sn.e: Returning the favour immediately would be ugly.

sn.s: Sería como decir que no quiero deber nada.
sn.e: It would be like saying I do not want to owe anything.

sn.s: Y aquí deber algo es estar unido.
sn.e: And here owing something is being connected.

sn.s: Nadie apunta los favores en un papel.
sn.e: Nobody writes the favours down on paper.

sn.s: Pero todos se acuerdan de todos.
sn.e: But everybody remembers everybody.

sn.s: Doña Carmen se acuerda de quién la ayudó.
sn.e: Doña Carmen remembers who helped her.

sn.s: Se acuerda de hace veinte años.
sn.e: She remembers from twenty years ago.

sn.s: "Esa señora me ayudó cuando nació Roberto."
sn.e: "That woman helped me when Roberto was born."

sn.s: Y por eso le hace favores hasta hoy.
sn.e: And that is why she does her favours to this day.

sn.s: Roberto me dice una cosa importante.
sn.e: Roberto tells me something important.

sn.s: "Si nunca pedís un favor, es raro."
sn.e: "If you never ask a favour, it's strange."

sn.s: "La gente piensa que no confiás."
sn.e: "People think you don't trust them."

sn.s: Eso me sorprende mucho.
sn.e: That surprises me a lot.

sn.s: Yo pensaba que pedir era molestar.
sn.e: I thought asking was imposing.

sn.s: Aquí pedir es lo contrario.
sn.e: Here asking is the opposite.

sn.s: Pedir es decir que uno confía.
sn.e: Asking is saying that you trust.

sn.s: El que no pide nada no da nada.
sn.e: The one who asks for nothing gives nothing.

sn.s: Y el que no da nada está solo.
sn.e: And the one who gives nothing is alone.

sn.s: Entonces empiezo a pedir favores.
sn.e: So I start asking for favours.

sn.s: Le pido a Roberto que me acompañe al banco.
sn.e: I ask Roberto to come with me to the bank.

sn.s: Le pido a doña Chepa que me guarde una bolsa.
sn.e: I ask doña Chepa to keep a bag for me.

sn.s: Le pido a doña Marta una receta.
sn.e: I ask doña Marta for a recipe.

sn.s: Todos dicen que sí sin dudar.
sn.e: They all say yes without hesitating.

sn.s: Y todos me piden algo después.
sn.e: And they all ask me for something later.

sn.s: Y así uno se va metiendo en la calle.
sn.e: And that is how you work your way into the street.

sn.s: No por hablar bien.
sn.e: Not by speaking well.

sn.s: Por deber y que le deban.
sn.e: By owing and being owed.
